name: Bifidobacterium longum
short_description: Gram-positive, strictly anaerobic, non-motile, non-sporing rod (2-5 um) that is characteristically bifid - forked into a Y, or club-ended and branched, which is exactly what gives the genus its name. One of the first colonisers of a newborn's gut, it ferments the human-milk oligosaccharides the baby cannot digest and releases acetate and lactate that acidify the gut and keep pathogens out.

textbook.1: PASS - the diagnostic bifid morphology is unmistakable: a slender rod whose lower pole forks into a clear Y with two blunt club-shaped arms, exactly as the reference demands, and emphatically not a plain straight sausage. House style matched: MUTED dusty educational palette (ochre-olive wall, warm cream cytoplasm, blue-violet nucleoid fibrils, muted teal ribosome speckles), THIN clean outlines rather than heavy cartoon strokes, soft dimensional shading, neutral dark-charcoal background filling the frame edge-to-edge. Envelope is correctly Gram-positive - ONE thick peptidoglycan band over ONE plasma membrane, no outer membrane, no periplasm, no LPS. Only a few short straight adhesive pili; no flagella, no endospore, no mesosome, no eukaryotic organelles, nothing floating outside the cell. No text, no scale bar, no border. Chosen as the label base.

sem.1: PASS - photorealistic false-colour SEM look: a single warm-beige specimen on a charcoal substrate, crisply forked into a Y whose three ends are all visibly swollen and club-shaped, with fine short surface filaments (pili) and a believable granular cell-surface texture. Surface only, no internal structures (correct for SEM), shallow depth of field with two softly blurred neighbouring cells that read as context rather than a dense clump. Closely matches the real micrograph. No flagella, no spores, no text, no scale bar, no border.

3d.1: PASS - natural, believable biological tints rather than near-monochrome or neon: warm translucent cream cytoplasm, dusty ochre-olive wall, a distinct teal plasma-membrane line, a pale mint exopolysaccharide haze and blue-violet nucleoid fibrils with fine teal ribosome granules. Presented as an upright Y with two club-tipped arms and a long cutaway that shows the single-membrane Gram-positive envelope correctly. Soft global illumination and subsurface scattering on a clean dark studio background, gentle rim light. No flagella, no endospore, no outer membrane, no text, no border.

watercolor.1: PASS - hand-painted naturalist plate in the house watercolour style: warm aged paper fills the ENTIRE frame corner-to-corner (no sheet-on-a-surface, no mat, no frame, no drop shadow), with only a soft pale blue-green wash halo laid directly on the paper behind the specimen. Fine ink linework over rich translucent washes, each structure its own gentle tint (ochre-olive wall, violet membrane line and nucleoid, sage ribosome discs, cream cytoplasm). The bifid fork with three club ends is clear, fine adhesive pili are drawn as short straight hairs, and there is no flagellum, no spore and no text. Labels applied as black ink on a paper-coloured halo.

reference: PASS - Wikimedia Commons electron micrograph 'Bifidobacterium longum en microscopie electronique' (Julie6301, CC BY-SA 3.0) genuinely shows the organism: slender rods forking into clean Y shapes with blunt club-tipped arms, no flagella and no spores. The Commons original is only 400x253 px, so the normalised 1080-square master is a soft upscale, and the uploader declares 'own work' without naming an instrument or laboratory - the licence is clear, the chain of custody is thinner than a journal figure. It was cleaned with edit_image.py (real-02) to isolate one forked specimen, strip the soft edges and apply a warm beige false-colour on charcoal; that cleaned version is a generative-AI recomposition faithful to the source morphology rather than raw instrument data, and the untouched download is kept beside it for provenance. Honest caveat recorded in the log.
decision: muted refined cutaway; the Y-fork, both club ends, the single thick Gram-positive wall, plasma membrane, nucleoid, ribosomes, exopolysaccharide haze and adhesive pili are all labelled - the clearest plate for teaching why the genus is called Bifidobacterium
false-colour surface-only SEM of a single forked specimen with club tips; matches the real micrograph closely and shows the branching in three dimensions
natural biological tints, upright Y with a long cutaway through the correct single-membrane Gram-positive envelope; labelled
full-bleed aged-paper naturalist plate, first attempt already coloured and edge-to-edge; labelled with black-on-paper ink
Wikimedia CC BY-SA 3.0 electron micrograph of forked B. longum, cleaned to a single specimen and false-coloured; low-resolution source and thin provenance noted honestly
